title: Felix and the Witness
premise: True-crime podcaster Sable Eastwick has spent seven years covering the disappearance of a child from the tidal flats of Greywater Bay, a case officially closed when the boy's foster brother confessed and drowned himself. Then a letter arrives, postmarked one day after the confession-writer's funeral, claiming the confession was coerced by the town's beloved harbormaster, who has been quietly silencing witnesses for decades. As Sable digs, they realize the letter-writer is still alive, hiding inside the very community Sable must charm to get answers. The investigation climaxes when the tide exposes the harbormaster's buried evidence, forcing Sable to choose between protecting their new source and exposing the truth; in the end, the witness testifies, the harbormaster falls, and Sable, once an outsider, finally belongs to the town that almost destroyed them both.
about_author: Dominic Coldharbour is a former coastal news reporter who spent a decade covering small-town inquests along the northern seaboard before turning to fiction. He writes in a converted boathouse and claims every mystery he tells begins with something the water gave back.

chapters.title: The Day After the Funeral
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. While recording the final episode of their podcast series on the Greywater Bay confession, Sable receives an anonymous letter insisting the drowned man was innocent. The emotional beat is unease: Sable has built a career on other people's endings, and this letter suggests one of them was a lie.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable travels to Greywater Bay, posing as a journalist doing an anniversary piece, and finds a town rehearsed in grief and defensive of its harbormaster, Aldous Crane. A chance encounter with a woman who burns the letter's copy hints the fear is real. The beat: the town is a locked room.

chapters.title: The Confession That Drowned
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reconstructs the original case through old files and the podcast archive, finding timeline inconsistencies no one pursued because the confession ended the questions. A retired deputy lets slip that Crane 'handled' the interview. The beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: A Town of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the letter-writer, revealed to be innkeeper Maren Quill, watching Sable from a distance. Maren was the child's teacher and saw something the night of the disappearance, but Crane destroyed her credibility years ago. Her beat: longing to speak, terror of the cost.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Crane befriends Sable, offering access and charm, and subtly warns them off 'reopening wounds.' Sable realizes Crane suspects who they really are. The beat: the antagonist's power shown as warmth, making his menace worse.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable's rental is ransacked and their research notes stolen; a local teenager who helped them is threatened. Maren anonymously leaves a page of the missing notes at Sable's door. The beat: fear hardens into resolve; the two investigators nearly touch.

chapters.title: The Night Maren Saw
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, a flashback chapter. Maren recounts the night of the disappearance: she saw Crane's truck on the flats with the child alive in the cab, and stayed silent after Crane ruined her reputation. The beat: guilt and the corrosive arithmetic of self-preservation.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sable and Maren finally meet in the marsh at low tide, where erosion has exposed a buried lockbox containing the child's belongings and Crane's ledger of payoffs. Crane's men are closing in. The beat: alliance formed at the moment of maximum danger.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Climax, Sable's POV. At a storm-battered town meeting called to run Sable out, Maren stands and testifies; Crane attempts to discredit her, but the ledger and a live-streamed recording turn the room. Crane is arrested as the storm floods the harbor. The beat: truth spoken at last, at real cost.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, weeks later. The case is reopened and officially unsolved no more; the child's family finally buries him. Sable releases the final episode, then stays in Greywater Bay, invited for the first time to stay. The beat: quiet resolution—truth cost everything and gave back a place to stand.
